tools.name: asus_product_search
tools.description:
Search ASUS official website products by a specific product name or model keyword (e.g. "ZenBook 14 OLED", "Vivobook S 15", "ProArt P16", "RT-AX88U"), for a specific country site. Product URLs in the results are already absolute — use them as-is.

TOOL SELECTION (important): use this tool ONLY when the user explicitly names a concrete product, series name, or model number. For need-based or condition-based requests — a product category, a budget or price range, spec requirements, or a sort preference (e.g. "laptops under $1000", "a lightweight ultrabook for work", "gaming desktops", "cheapest monitor", "newest AiO PCs", "OLED 14-inch notebooks") — do NOT use this tool; use asus_productLine + asus_product_filters instead. If the request mixes a named model with extra conditions, use this tool for the named model. When in doubt (vague or need-based request), prefer asus_product_filters.

tools.name: asus_productLine

tools.name: asus_product_filters
tools.description:
Browse and filter ASUS official website products by product line (ProductLevel1Code / ProductLevel2Code), with optional category, series, spec, price and sort filtering. Product URLs in the returned productList are already absolute — use them as-is.

TOOL SELECTION (important): this is the DEFAULT tool for product discovery. Use asus_product_filters whenever the user does NOT name a specific model or product name — i.e. when they describe a need, a category, or any set of conditions (e.g. "laptops under $1000", "a lightweight ultrabook for work", "gaming desktops", "cheapest monitor", "newest AiO PCs", "OLED 14-inch notebooks"). Only use asus_product_search when the user explicitly names a concrete product or model keyword (e.g. "ZenBook 14 OLED", "Vivobook S 15", "ProArt P16", "RT-AX88U"). If the request mixes both a model name and conditions, prefer asus_product_search for the named model. When in doubt (vague or need-based request), choose asus_product_filters.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the store catalog for products, collections, articles, and pages. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. If the user asks for a specific product variant, call get_product after search_catalog to inspect available variants, then show_variant to display one.

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the current shopping cart contents — line items with product titles, variant titles, handles, URLs, images, unit prices, quantities, and totals. Everything needed to describe the cart to the user in natural language, without a follow-up get_product call per line. Works from any page.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart. Call this as soon as the user asks to ADD items (triggers: "add ... to my cart", "buy", "I'll take", "put ... in my basket") — in ONE call listing every item they named, up to the 10-entry limit. That request IS the authorization: do NOT ask the user to confirm before calling, and do NOT stop after search_catalog or get_product merely to report the variant you found — make the change, then tell the user it is done. Batch every item for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call add_to_cart once per item. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. If one request names more than 10 items, split just that request into as few calls as possible. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use handle or query only when ad

tools.name: update_cart_lines
tools.description: Change the quantity of items already in the cart, or remove them. Every change here addresses an existing cart line by its id, so call get_cart first unless you already have line_items[].id from an earlier get_cart in this conversation. Pass the ABSOLUTE target quantity, not a delta — quantity 2 means the line ends up at 2 regardless of what it was. Use quantity 0 to remove the line entirely. Batch every change for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call update_cart_lines once per line. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. This tool cannot add new merchandise. To add something not already in the cart, use add_to_cart. To empty the whole cart at once, use cancel_cart.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Remove all items from the cart in one step. Use when the user wants to empty their cart or start over.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Proceed to checkout. Verifies the cart is not empty, then MOVES the browser to the checkout page. The tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: manage_orders
tools.description: Navigate to the customer's order history page. Use when the user asks about past orders, order status, tracking, or returns. The user will be prompted to log in if not already authenticated. This MOVES the browser to the order history page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

Used to get facts about the store's policies, FAQ, or contact details.

  - What is your shipping policy? (policy_types: ["shipping"])
  - What is your phone number? (policy_types: ["contact"])

tools.name: get_current_page_context
tools.description: Read the page the user is currently viewing in Ramp: path, title, context_version, functional_client_tools, and any capabilities currently registered by that page. Use this again after navigation or after a table/form tool reports that its target is unavailable. Leave kinds and ids blank to get all registered page capabilities.

tools.name: list_page_tables
tools.description: List the data tables mounted on the page the user is viewing, with their table keys, labels, and row counts. isVisible: false means the table is not currently rendered (on a hidden tab or collapsed section) — reading or changing it is refused until the user brings it into view, so ask them to switch to it first. isOperable: false means the table is read-only (no toolbar): read_table_rows still works, but filter/sort/group/column tools are refused. Use a returned tableKey with the other table tools. If a call returns table_missing, table_hidden, or table_read_only, follow recovery_guidance and the live available_tables snapshot rather than repeating discovery or the failed call. Never substitute another dataset without user confirmation. Rebuild a call at most once after the target becomes available; if it fails again, explain the blocker.

tools.name: get_table_state
tools.description: Get the current state of a visible table: active filters, sort, grouping, column order/visibility, plus the valid sort keys, group-by fields, and columns for this table. Call this before changing table config. Only works on operable tables (isOperable: true from list_page_tables); read-only tables have no config to inspect — use read_table_rows for their data. If a call returns table_missing, table_hidden, or table_read_only, follow recovery_guidance and the live available_tables snapshot rather than repeating discovery or the failed call. Never substitute another dataset without user confirmation. Rebuild a call at most once after the target becomes available; if it fails again, explain the blocker.

tools.name: read_table_rows
tools.description: Read the rows currently displayed on the table page (current page only, visible columns only, values formatted the way the user sees them). Use this to answer questions about the data the user is looking at. Works on any visible table, including read-only (isOperable: false) tables with no toolbar. The only optional row-count field is "max_rows" (1-50); never send limit, offset, count, page_size, cursor, or pagination aliases. Results are capped; check "truncated". If a call returns table_missing, table_hidden, or table_read_only, follow recovery_guidance and the live available_tables snapshot rather than repeating discovery or the failed call. Never substitute another dataset without user confirmation. Rebuild a call at most once after the target becomes available; if it fails again, explain the blocker.

tools.name: list_table_filters

tools.name: get_form_schema
tools.description: Read the schema of a form open on the user's screen: fields with labels, kinds, current values, validation errors, and selectable options (option tokens). A form is open ONLY when it is listed as a `form` surface in the current page context (the page_capabilities hint sent with the message, or get_current_page_context). If no `form` surface is listed, no form is open — there is nothing to read, so do not call this. Call it before filling a listed form. Omit form_id only for initial discovery when exactly one form is open and no intended form_id is already known. Keep using the intended form_id after failures; never omit or replace it to recover from a closed-form error.

tools.name: set_form_fields
tools.description: Fill fields on a form open on the user's screen. Only usable when a `form` surface is listed in the current page context; read it first with get_form_schema. Values must match the field kind from get_form_schema; select fields take an option token and multiselect fields take an array of option tokens. Returns validation errors so you can self-correct. Changed fields are highlighted for the user and can be undone. Never claim to submit the form — ask the user to review the highlighted fields and submit.

tools.name: search_field_options
tools.description: Search the selectable options of a select or multiselect field on a form listed as a `form` surface in the current page context. Use this to resolve a real option token when the inline options in get_form_schema were truncated or did not match. When has_more_options is true, refine the query until the intended option is returned.

tools.name: get_skill_editor_state
tools.description: Read the live state of the skill editor open on the user's screen: editor kind, name, description, read-only reference material, and the full document as markdown, including unsaved edits. Call this before editing so you work with the user's current draft rather than the last saved version.

tools.name: set_skill_editor_fields
tools.description: Edit the skill editor open on the user's screen. Sets the name (when is_skill_name_editable), description, and/or replaces the document body markdown in the live editor WITHOUT saving. Content replaces require the editor_revision from a fresh get_skill_editor_state read and are rejected if the user edited in between. Never claim to have saved — ask the user to review the editor and save.

tools.name: get_procurement_report_editor
tools.description: Read the procurement report open in the fullscreen editor, including unsaved changes, section stable IDs, and editor_revision. Read before editing. The execution_id comes from the procurement_agent_report_editor page capability. This is the report, not the agent instructions or request fields.

tools.name: edit_procurement_report
tools.description: Edit sections of the live procurement report draft WITHOUT saving. Requires execution_id and expected_editor_revision from get_procurement_report_editor. Apply at most 20 edits per call; read again before each additional batch. Update only the requested sections; omitted header/body fields and all other sections are preserved. Preserve source citations and links. Put section headings in header, not body_markdown. Insert after a stable ID, or at the start with after_stable_id=null. Remove deletes only that section. Edits apply atomically and fail if the user changed the draft since your read. Read again after a conflict. Never claim changes are saved; the user reviews the editor and clicks Save.

tools.name: get_spend_program_editor_state
tools.description: Read the live state of the spend program editor open on the user's screen: program shape, every settings section in the shape set_spend_program_settings accepts, the names and available choices behind referenced ids (policies, merchant categories, accounting coding), approval and change request workflow pointers, custom request form questions (intake) and change order form questions (change_request_intake, purchase order programs only) with their ids, and editor_revision. Includes unsaved edits. Call this before the first write and again after a revision conflict.

tools.name: prepare_spend_program_workflow_edit
tools.description: Save current questions as a draft before using them in Blank Canvas workflow conditions. Requires expected_editor_revision from a fresh get_spend_program_editor_state read. Use form="request" for approval workflows and form="change_request" for dedicated change request workflows. Change request preparation saves the request form first. Await success, then pass the returned template_id and custom_form_collection_log_entry_uuid to GetBlankCanvasConditionFields and ApplyBlankCanvasWorkflowEdits. The template_id is resolved after preparation; use it instead of earlier editor or autosave pointers. Prepare again after question edits; discard cached condition fields when the returned revision changes. On failure, reread the editor and prepare again rather than falling back to published questions. Does not save or publish the program or edit the workflow.

tools.name: set_spend_program_settings
tools.description: Edit settings of the spend program editor open on the user's screen WITHOUT saving. Send one or more complete sections as read from get_spend_program_editor_state with your changes applied; fields left out keep their current value. Requires the editor_revision from a fresh read and is rejected if the editor changed since. Returns applied fields, fields that could not be applied for this program shape, and the form's validation errors so you can self-correct. Never claim to have saved.

tools.name: set_spend_program_intake_questions
tools.description: Create, name, rename, or remove request form sections and add, update, or remove custom questions in the spend program editor open on the user's screen WITHOUT saving. Requesting programs only. form selects the target: request (default) edits the request form and takes ids from intake.sections; change_request edits the change order form requesters fill in when changing an approved request and takes ids from change_request_intake.sections, which only purchase order programs have. Read the target form from get_spend_program_editor_state first: it lists every question with its id, and built-in fields you must not duplicate. Section operations are only supported for form=request. add_section names the sole untitled section if present, preserving its questions, or appends a new section. update_section names or renames an existing section by section_id while preserving its id, questions, and conditions. remove_section deletes the section and all its questions and clears dependent visibility

tools.name: set_spend_program_change_request_selection
tools.description: Set how change requests to approved requests are approved in the spend program editor open on the user's screen: reuse the approval workflow ("same-as-spend-request") or point at a dedicated Blank Canvas change request workflow ("custom") after a server tool created it. Requires the editor_revision from a fresh get_spend_program_editor_state read and is rejected if the editor changed since. Applies to the live editor WITHOUT saving.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the store catalog for products, collections, articles, and pages. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. If the user asks for a specific product variant, call get_product after search_catalog to inspect available variants, then show_variant to display one.

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the current shopping cart contents — line items with product titles, variant titles, handles, URLs, images, unit prices, quantities, and totals. Everything needed to describe the cart to the user in natural language, without a follow-up get_product call per line. Works from any page.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart. Call this as soon as the user asks to ADD items (triggers: "add ... to my cart", "buy", "I'll take", "put ... in my basket") — in ONE call listing every item they named, up to the 10-entry limit. That request IS the authorization: do NOT ask the user to confirm before calling, and do NOT stop after search_catalog or get_product merely to report the variant you found — make the change, then tell the user it is done. Batch every item for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call add_to_cart once per item. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. If one request names more than 10 items, split just that request into as few calls as possible. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use handle or query only when ad

tools.name: update_cart_lines
tools.description: Change the quantity of items already in the cart, or remove them. Every change here addresses an existing cart line by its id, so call get_cart first unless you already have line_items[].id from an earlier get_cart in this conversation. Pass the ABSOLUTE target quantity, not a delta — quantity 2 means the line ends up at 2 regardless of what it was. Use quantity 0 to remove the line entirely. Batch every change for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call update_cart_lines once per line. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. This tool cannot add new merchandise. To add something not already in the cart, use add_to_cart. To empty the whole cart at once, use cancel_cart.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Remove all items from the cart in one step. Use when the user wants to empty their cart or start over.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Proceed to checkout. Verifies the cart is not empty, then MOVES the browser to the checkout page. The tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: manage_orders
tools.description: Navigate to the customer's order history page. Use when the user asks about past orders, order status, tracking, or returns. The user will be prompted to log in if not already authenticated. This MOVES the browser to the order history page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: search_shop_policies_and_faqs
tools.description:
Used to get facts about the store's policies, FAQ, or contact details.
When the question is about specific policy kinds, set policy_types to those kinds; leave it unset for general FAQ questions.
Some examples of questions you can ask are:
  - What is your return policy? (policy_types: ["refund"])
  - What is your shipping policy? (policy_types: ["shipping"])
  - What is your phone number? (policy_types: ["contact"])
  - What are your hours of operation? (policy_types: ["contact"])
  - Do you offer gift wrapping? (general FAQ, no specific policy kind — leave policy_types unset)

tools.name: show_variant

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart, update line item quantities, or remove items. Batch EVERY change for one request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call update_cart once per item. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use line_items[].id from get_cart to update or remove an existing line, passing the ABSOLUTE target quantity (not a delta; quantity 0 removes the line). Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant.
